newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-O'BRIEN STEPS INTO SAMPRAS'S SHOES AND WINS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-O'BRIEN STEPS INTO SAMPRAS'S SHOES AND WINS.

text.p: Alex O'Brien stepped in for world number one Pete Sampras to lead the United States to a 2-1 win over Croatia in the World Team Cup on Wednesday.
When Sampras was forced to pull out of the tournament with a strained thigh muscle in the morning, O'Brien, a doubles specialist, was called up to face Sasa Hirszon in a vital singles clash.
O'Brien deputised well, crushing the Croatian 6-1 6-2 to level the tie at 1-1.
World number four Goran Ivanisevic had given Croatia a 1-0 lead with a workmanlike 6-2 2-6 6-3 win over Michael Chang.
O'Brien then joined Jonathan Stark to cap a successful day with 6-3 7-6 victory over Ivanisevic and Hirszon in the deciding doubles to keep alive U.S. hopes of a fifth title.
The day had begun well enough for Ivanisevic and Hirszon. They completed their rain delayed doubles rubber against the Czech Republic in the morning to take the tie 2-1.

"This tournament is great preparation for the French (Open) and when you beat a French Open champion and one of the best clay court players in the world like Chang, it boosts your confidence," said Ivanisevic, who was playing in only his second tournament following a three-week layoff with a broken finger.
"I feel good and I'm playing well but I don't want to put too much pressure on myself. The French Open is a different world."
Chang's build-up to the French Open has been far from promising.
Since winning the U.S. Clay Court championhip last month he has struggled on the slow surface, losing in the first round in Atlanta and Rome.
"It's actually getting better, I feel like things are starting to come together," said Chang, the 1989 French Open champion. "Even though I lost I feel I played better than I did in my first match."

Sampras, who injured his thigh in his opening match against Australia's Mark Philippoussis on Monday, said he would leave for Paris on Thursday and would play in the French Open, the only grand slam title to elude him.
"I don't feel the injury when I walk but doctors advised me not to come back too soon or I could make it worse," he said."I'm planning on playing in Paris."
Australia kept their unbeaten record intact by romping to a 3-0 win over the Czech Republic.
Philippoussis beat Bodhan Ulihrach 6-4 4-6 6-3 while Mark Woodforde defeated Petr Korda 3-6 7-5 6-1.
Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge, the world's top ranked doubles team, completed the sweep with a 6-4 6-3 win over Martin Damm and Daniel Vacek.
Australia lead the red group standings with 2-0 record, followed by the U.S. and Croatia with 1-1.
